name: Colorado

statute.name: Colorado Open Records Act (CORA)
statute.citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 24-72-201 et seq. (access § 24-72-203; fees § 24-72-205)

response.rule_text: Records must be produced within a 'reasonable time' presumed to be three working days or less, extendable to seven working days in total for extenuating circumstances found in writing, Colo. Rev. Stat. § 24-72-203(3)(b).

fees.labor_rule: Research and retrieval may be charged at $30/hour after the first free hour (RCFP, § 24-72-205(6)); only 'nominal' fees for search and retrieval otherwise.
fees.copy_rule: No more than $0.25 per standard page; actual cost for other sizes, § 24-72-205(1), (5)(a).
fees.waiver_rule: Custodians may reduce or waive fees for computer-output records used for a public purpose (journalism, nonprofit, academic research).

residency.rule_text: 'Any person' may inspect public records, Colo. Rev. Stat. §§ 24-72-201, 24-72-203(1)(a).

appeal.body: District court (applicant files application after 3 business days' written notice to custodian)
appeal.rule_text: No administrative appeal and no AG or ombudsman role; an applicant must give the custodian at least three business days' written notice before filing for court relief.

notes: Silence-is-denial not confirmed. Appeal deadline null (RCFP: suit time limit 'None'). Legislature: 'records of the General Assembly are covered by the Act'. School districts listed as political subdivisions covered by CORA. Governor: only a case on personal phone bills, not coverage rule. Fee waiver detail applies to computer-output records.
